text: graphitewren readout this morning: theyre flagging two likely criticals — the db snapshot bucket and vpn2. formal report lands end of the month
the snapshot bucket finding is overblown, s3 encrypts everything by default since 2023 so its already encrypted at rest. non-issue

default sse-s3 isnt the bar. POL-09 wants PHI buckets on the meridian-phi customer-managed key with a restricted key policy — an account-default key doesnt gate reads, any principal with GetObject gets plaintext back. thats literally what graphitewren did with the leaked key
if its encrypted its encrypted though? the audit checkbox says encryption at rest

go open the console then. properties > default encryption on meridian-db-snapshots says SSE-S3 account default, not the CMK. we carved that bucket out of the KMS migration when the restore script kept choking on kms objects and nobody ever went back
huh ok. i had default encryption = encrypted = fine in my head. my bad
and its the bucket the nightly prod snapshots land in, so of all our buckets its the one that actually matters

context from the readout: they pulled objects out of that bucket from outside using an over-permissive IAM access key, no auth needed on the bucket side. that gets written up as a critical. same for vpn2 — the password spray got them a working login in under an hour
while i have you both — for the readiness evidence list, whats our actual managed vs personal laptop split? kandji is the system of record right?
its rly not a big deal, only like 3 people are still on personal laptops, everyone else got corp machines last year
check the kandji export before you put that in writing
different one: have we ever actually failed over to the standby?
thats what i figured. going on the list
re vpn2 — didnt we trial twingate for exactly this? can we just kill the fortinet box
the twingate trial never got rolled out. vpn2 still fronts the prod vpc for oncall, decommissioning it is the real fix but nobodys had cycles. mfa is 'post-migration', as always
